color.scale.magma.label: Magma
color.scale.magma.description: Black to cream through violet and orange.
color.scale.inferno.label: Inferno
color.scale.inferno.description: Black to pale yellow through red.
color.scale.cividis.label: Cividis
color.scale.cividis.description: Blue to yellow, built to read the same to a deuteranope.
color.scale.turbo.label: Turbo
color.scale.turbo.description: Rainbow colours, ordered so the lightness still climbs.
color.scale.greys.label: Greys
color.scale.greys.description: Light to black, for a figure that will be photocopied.
color.scale.cool-warm.label: Cool to warm
color.scale.cool-warm.description: Blue through pale yellow to red.
color.scale.blue-red.label: Blue to red

color.scale.rainbow.label: Rainbow
color.scale.rainbow.description: Blue through green and yellow to red. Orders nothing in grey.
download.formatHelp: A PNG is a picture of the figure, which is what a slide, a chat window or an issue accepts. An SVG is the figure itself: every line stays sharp however far it is enlarged, and it can still be edited afterwards.
download.resolutionHelp: How many pixels are painted for each pixel of the figure on screen. Two is right for a slide, three or four for print. An SVG carries no resolution of its own, so it is saved sharp at every size.
download.resolutionExample: A figure 640 pixels wide on screen is saved 1280 pixels wide.
download.noFigure: There is no figure on the page to save yet.
download.hintRasterSvg: An SVG holding a picture of {pixels}: a 3D scene has no vector form.
download.hintSvg: An SVG stays sharp at any size, so the resolution does not apply. Drawn {pixels}.

slides.noAddress: This slide frames a tool, but carries no address.

structure.guide.atom.title: Pointer on an atom
structure.guide.atom.group: Attach a phenyl; Me, Et, Boc, TMS… work too
structure.guide.atom.applyOrForget: Apply or forget what was typed
structure.guide.atom.chain: Attach a chain of that many carbons
structure.guide.atom.spin: Make it a triplet, then a singlet
structure.guide.atom.note: What is typed shows black for an element, blue for a group, grey while incomplete and red when unknown.
structure.guide.bond.title: Pointer on a bond
structure.guide.bond.ring: Fuse a ring of that size
structure.guide.anywhere.title: Anywhere
structure.guide.anywhere.paste: Paste a molfile, a SMILES or an idCode
structure.guide.anywhere.note: Keys act once the drawing has been clicked. On empty canvas, a key picks the tool whose tooltip shows it.
structure.guide.selecting.title: Selecting
structure.guide.selecting.queryFeatures: Edit the query features of an atom, a bond or the selection
structure.guide.selecting.note: These need the Select tool, which Space picks.
structure.guide.stereochemistry.title: Stereochemistry
structure.guide.stereochemistry.note: Pink bonds flag a stereocentre with too little or too much information. Draw an up or down bond with its narrow end on the centre, then use the enhanced stereo tool to say whether the drawing is this enantiomer (abs), both of them (&) or one of the two (or).
structure.help.hoverToolbar: Hover a toolbar button to see what it does and its key.
structure.tool.clear.name: Clear
structure.tool.cleanUp.name: Clean up
structure.tool.cleanUp.description: Redraw the structure with fresh 2D coordinates. With part of it selected, the rest keeps its layout.
structure.tool.select.name: Select
structure.tool.select.description: Drag around atoms to select them: hold Alt for a rectangle, Shift to add to the selection. Drag a selection to move it, Shift-drag to copy it.
structure.tool.unknownConfiguration.name: Unknown configuration
structure.tool.unknownConfiguration.desc: Click a stereocentre to mark its configuration as unknown; click again to undo it.
structure.tool.delete.name: Delete
structure.tool.delete.description: Click an atom or a bond to delete it.
structure.tool.singleBond.name: Single bond
structure.tool.singleBond.description: Click empty space for a new bond, or drag from an atom. Clicking a bond again makes it double, then triple.
structure.tool.upBond.name: Up bond
structure.tool.upBond.description: Wedged stereo bond, pointing toward the viewer. Its narrow end goes on the stereocentre.
structure.tool.positiveCharge.name: Positive charge
structure.tool.positiveCharge.descriptio: Click an atom to raise its charge by one.
structure.tool.undo.name: Undo
structure.tool.zoomAndRotate.name: Zoom and rotate
structure.tool.zoomAndRotate.description: Press where the centre should be, then drag up or down to zoom and sideways to rotate. With a selection, only that part moves.
structure.tool.atomMapping.name: Atom mapping
structure.tool.atomMapping.description: Drag from a reactant atom to the same atom in a product: both get the same number. Click a mapped atom to unmap it.
structure.tool.enhancedStereo.name: Enhanced stereo
structure.tool.enhancedStereo.descriptio: Click a stereo bond to say what its centre means: abs, this enantiomer; &, both (racemic); or, one of the two. Press the button again to switch between the three.
structure.tool.text.name: Text
structure.tool.text.description: Place a text label in the drawing.
structure.tool.chain.name: Chain
structure.tool.chain.description: Drag from empty space or from an atom to draw a zigzag carbon chain.
structure.tool.downBond.name: Down bond
structure.tool.downBond.description: Hashed stereo bond, pointing away from the viewer. Its narrow end goes on the stereocentre.
structure.tool.negativeCharge.name: Negative charge
structure.tool.negativeCharge.descriptio: Click an atom to lower its charge by one.
structure.tool.anyAtom.name: Any atom
structure.tool.anyAtom.description: Pick any element, isotope, valence or radical in a dialog, then click to place it or to change an atom. Alt-click an atom to edit its own properties.
structure.tool.ring3.name: 3-membered ring
structure.tool.ring3.description: Click empty space for a new ring, a bond to fuse one onto it, or an atom for a spiro ring.
structure.tool.ring5.name: 5-membered ring
structure.tool.ring5.description: Click empty space for a new ring, a bond to fuse one onto it, or an atom for a spiro ring.

structure.tool.ring7.description: Click empty space for a new ring, a bond to fuse one onto it, or an atom for a spiro ring.

structure.tool.silicon.name: Silicon
structure.tool.silicon.description: Click empty space for a new Si atom, or an atom to turn it into Si.
structure.tool.phosphorus.name: Phosphorus
structure.tool.phosphorus.description: Click empty space for a new P atom, or an atom to turn it into P.
structure.tool.sulfur.name: Sulfur

molecule3d.solventProbeHelp: Radius of the solvent sphere rolled over the atoms. 1.4 Å is a water molecule; a larger probe smooths the surface and closes the narrow pockets.
molecule3d.tpsaHelp: Topological polar surface area (Ertl): the area contributed by nitrogen, oxygen and their hydrogens, computed from the structure by openchemlib. It does not depend on the conformer or the probe.
molecule3d.couldNotDraw: The viewer could not draw this
molecule3d.gesture.rollDrag: Rotate in the plane of the screen
molecule3d.gesture.rollKeys: Rotate in the plane, while held
molecule3d.helpNote: Keys act while the pointer is over the molecule. On a Mac, Ctrl is the Control key, not ⌘. With a measuring tool on, a click picks an atom.
orbital.couldNotDraw: This orbital could not be drawn
orbital.showAxes: Show the x, y, z axes
orbital.axesBody: Draw x, y and z through the nucleus. The label names an orbital by where its lobes sit against them.
orbital.axesExample: four lobes between the y and z axes, none on either.
orbital.resetBody: Back to the angle and zoom the orbital opened on. A change of orbital keeps whatever view you have turned it to.
viewer.capability.noWindow: The 3D viewer needs a browser window.
viewer.capability.noContext: This browser could not create a WebGL context, so the 3D viewer cannot start. Enable hardware acceleration, or update the graphics driver.
viewer.capability.noFloatTextures: This graphics driver has no floating-point textures, so computed orbitals are built on the processor instead. Everything works, but each orbital takes a few seconds.
viewer.capability.ready: This browser can render the 3D viewer and computed orbitals.
conformers.strategyDetail.adaptive-rando: Draws torsions at random but steers away from the combinations that already collided, which covers a flexible molecule fastest.
conformers.strategyDetail.likely-random: Draws torsions at random from the torsion database, weighted by how often each angle is seen in crystal structures.
conformers.strategyDetail.pure-random: Draws every torsion uniformly at random, ignoring how likely the angle is — the widest spread and the least realistic set.
conformers.strategyDetail.likely-systema: Walks the torsion combinations in decreasing likelihood, so the first conformers are the most probable ones and the set is reproducible.
